messages:
Alex Chen: FYI customer 'FinLedger' reporting a spike of 429s and elevated p95 latency since ~09:10 UTC. They say it started during a scheduled batch job but persists. attached logs show 429s with X-RateLimit-* headers missing.
Priya Rao: Ack. Any customer request IDs or example headers? missing X-RateLimit headers usually means the request was rejected before the gateway applied limits.
Alex Chen: Here’s a sample (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"model":"rdw-alpha-1","input":"..."}
Response: 429 Too Many Requests
Body: {"error":"quota exceeded"}
No X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining in response headers
```
Miguel Santos: Interesting — if the response lacks rate-limit headers it might be a quota check at auth layer or billing block. @BillingBot any recent billing events for FinLedger?
BillingBot: FinLedger invoice for March was 'previously due' but customer has an open support ticket; no automatic suspension configured.
Tara Nguyen: Could also be our internal request router hitting a per-tenant global throttle (reserved capacity pools). If their dedicated pool was saturated the fallback path could be rejecting. Do we have route/model level metrics?
Priya Rao: I pulled the per-route counters from Grafana: model=rdw-alpha-1, route=/v1/generate. There's a ~10x spike in rejected_requests around 09:08–09:12. Successful_requests drop, 429s increase. I can paste the PromQL queries if useful.
Alex Chen: Please paste. Also customer says latency spiked to 3.5s p95 before 429s started.
Priya Rao: PromQL: `sum by (tenant_id) (rate(requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status!~"2.."}[1m]))` and `sum by (tenant_id) (rate(rejections_total{reason=~"quota|throttle"}[1m]))` — FinLedger tenant_id=tl_fin_987 shows a huge delta at 09:08.
Sam (L2): Quick checklist:
- Confirm API key maps to tl_fin_987
- Check usage spike / billing thresholds
- Check dedicated pool metrics (GPU saturation, queue depth)
- Inspect prefix/KV cache hit rate (to rule out cold cache causing load)
Alex Chen: Key maps correctly. Usage: they had a scheduled end-of-day run hitting many long sequences. Cache CPI dropped to 12% during the window.
Miguel Santos: Low cache hit + long sequences = more compute per request and more KV operations; could exhaust pooling and trigger queue-based rejection. Which rejection type are we seeing in logs? `reject_code=POOL_EXHAUSTION`?
Alex Chen: Log snip: `reject_reason=quota_enforced tenant=tl_fin_987 route=/v1/generate backend=dedicated-pool-3`
Tara Nguyen: That 'quota_enforced' suggests a guard in the routing layer saw tenant over its committed capacity. Could be burst exhaustion: they exceeded burst tokens and went into hard quota. Any per-tenant burst windows?
Priya Rao: Yes, billing config shows committed RPS=10, burst window tokens=50 over 60s. Their job hit ~120 concurrent requests for a minute.
Sam (L2): Steps to repro: ask customer to run a controlled smaller batch (10 concurrent) and capture X-Request-ID from responses. Also attach a curl sample they can run.
Alex Chen: Sent sample curl with `-H "X-Request-ID: test-429-{{ts}}"` and asked for timestamps. Also requested a HAR and the exact request pattern (seq len, concurrency).
Miguel Santos: For observability we should add a Grafana panel that attributes 429s by: tenant_id, route, model, and backend pool. Query: `sum by (tenant_id, route, model, pool) (rate(rejections_total{status="429"}[5m]))` — then stack by reason label. Add link and a short-runbook.
Tara Nguyen: Also create an alert: if tenant 5m rejection rate > 10 and error ratio > 0.1 for more than 3m, page on-call SRE and notify support. For now we can create a temporary dashboard tile and slack deeplink.
Priya Rao: I created a dashboard panel and posted link in #incidents: https://grafana.redwood/p/xyz?panelId=23&var-tenant=tl_fin_987 — shows clear spike and attribution to dedicated-pool-3.
Alex Chen: Customer confirms they scaled down and saw 429s stop after rate reduced. Want guidance on how to prevent: they asked about increasing burst tokens or scheduling windows.
Miguel Santos: Options: increase committed RPS or bump burst tokens. But that costs money. Alternatively, recommend client-side exponential backoff + rate limiter, and prefix caching where possible (shorter sequences or chunked requests).
Sam (L2): I'll draft an email with repro steps, recommended mitigations, and links to dashboard + instructions to request capacity bump.
Priya Rao: One more observability note — some 429s were misattributed earlier because our edge returns 503 for internal timeouts without rate headers. Recommend we add a fast-fail header `X-Rdw-Reject-Reason` populated at gateway so support can triage without digging logs.
Miguel Santos: +1. I'll file an infra ticket to add `X-Rdw-Reject-Reason` and ensure `X-RateLimit-*` are always present when applicable (even if body is 503).
OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of header-middleware queued for eng-runtime next week (ticket #ENG-4021).
Alex Chen: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks team — assigning follow-ups: @Sam (L2) will send the mitigation doc, @Miguel will own infra ticket, @Priya will keep dashboard tiling for 24h.
Sam (L2): Sending summary to FinLedger and copying billing. Will include recommended timeline for a short-term capacity bump and long-term policy.
BillingBot: Noted — will follow-up with sales on a provisional commit for increased capacity if customer requests.
Alex Chen: Marking as resolved for now; reopen if they see new 429s. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
